stories.headline: OpenAI launches GPT-5.4 with native computer use, 1M-token context, and record benchmarks
key_facts: OpenAI released GPT-5.4 on March 5 in three configurations: standard, Thinking (for ChatGPT Plus/Team/Pro), and Pro (for ChatGPT Pro and Enterprise), also available via API and Codex
On GDPval, a benchmark assessing knowledge work across 44 professions in nine industries, GPT-5.4 matches or exceeds human professionals in 83% of comparisons, up from 70.9% for GPT-5.2
On OSWorld-Verified desktop navigation benchmark, GPT-5.4 scores 75% success rate versus 72.4% human benchmark and GPT-5.2's 47.3%
API supports up to 1 million tokens context window, double GPT-5.3's 400,000 tokens, with premium pricing at 2x rate after 272,000 tokens
Introduces native computer use for software operation and file navigation, and a reworked tool-calling system with Tool Search that reduces token usage 47% on large agent systems
Hallucinations reduced by 33% fewer incorrect factual claims and 18% fewer overall errors versus GPT-5.2
OpenAI published a new Chain-of-Thought Controllability evaluation finding GPT-5.4 Thinking shows low ability to obscure its reasoning, suggesting CoT monitoring remains a useful safety tool
Release comes just two days after GPT-5.3 Instant and amid user cancellations over OpenAI's Pentagon contract

stories.headline: Claude Opus 4.6 finds 22 Firefox security vulnerabilities in two weeks, 14 high-severity
key_facts: Anthropic's Claude Opus 4.6 discovered 22 security vulnerabilities in Firefox during a two-week test in January 2026, with 14 classified as high-severity by Mozilla
Claude found its first vulnerability — a Use After Free flaw in Firefox's JavaScript engine — within 20 minutes of initial exploration
Anthropic scanned nearly 6,000 C++ files and submitted 112 unique reports to Mozilla's Bugzilla tracker, including roughly 90 non-security bugs like crashes and logic errors
The 14 high-severity bugs represent nearly one-fifth of all high-severity Firefox vulnerabilities remediated throughout 2025
All vulnerabilities were patched in Firefox 148.0, which rolled out to hundreds of millions of users
Anthropic spent approximately $4,000 in API credits attempting to generate proof-of-concept exploits, succeeding in only 2 cases that required sandbox removal to function
Anthropic also announced Claude Code Security, an automated vulnerability-discovery and patching tool in limited research preview for Enterprise and Team customers
Anthropic reported finding over 500 previously unknown vulnerabilities across open-source projects during broader Opus 4.6 testing

stories.headline: Cursor launches Automations: event-driven AI agents that run without developer prompts
key_facts: Cursor launched Automations on March 4, enabling always-on AI agents triggered by external events — Slack messages, GitHub pull requests, PagerDuty alerts, or scheduled timers
The system replaces the manual prompt-and-response model with a conveyor belt of digital triggers that activate coding agents without human initiation
Cursor's annualized revenue surpassed $2 billion in February 2026, doubling from $1 billion in November 2025
Enterprise customers now account for 60% of revenue, with Nvidia and Stripe deploying Cursor across thousands of engineers
Cursor is valued at $29.3 billion following a $2.3 billion funding round in late 2025
Use cases include automated code review, security scanning, incident response, bug triage, and weekly change summaries
Cursor positions Automations as the 'Third Era' of AI development — beyond autocomplete and chat toward continuous autonomous agent operation

stories.headline: Luma launches creative AI agents on Uni-1 model for end-to-end multimodal production
key_facts: Luma AI launched Luma Agents on March 5, built on its new Uni-1 model — a decoder-only autoregressive transformer trained on audio, video, image, language, and spatial reasoning
Agents handle end-to-end creative workflows from brief to final delivery across text, image, video, and audio, coordinating multiple external models
Integrates with 8+ external models including Luma's Ray 3.14, Google Veo 3, ByteDance Seedream, and ElevenLabs voice models
Launch partners include Publicis Groupe, Serviceplan Group, Adidas, and Mazda as enterprise customers
CEO Amit Jain described Uni-1 as a model that can 'think in language and imagine and render in pixels' — what Luma calls 'intelligence in pixels'
Beta tested with over 100 clients since December 2025; API access open now with gradual rollout

stories.headline: SoftBank seeks record $40 billion loan to finance OpenAI stake
key_facts: SoftBank is seeking a bridge loan of up to $40 billion — the largest dollar-denominated corporate borrowing ever — to finance its investment in OpenAI, per Bloomberg
The bridge loan has a tenor of about 12 months, with four lenders including JPMorgan Chase underwriting the facility
SoftBank's $30 billion investment in OpenAI is part of a broader $110 billion funding round that also includes $30 billion from Nvidia and $50 billion from Amazon
SoftBank has already invested over $30 billion in OpenAI prior to this round, bringing its total commitment past $60 billion
S&P lowered SoftBank's credit outlook, citing danger that its OpenAI investments may hurt the company's liquidity and credit quality
The loan highlights founder Masayoshi Son's aggressive positioning of SoftBank as central to the AI infrastructure boom

stories.headline: UK launches £40 million Fundamental AI Research Lab targeting hallucination and reasoning flaws
key_facts: The UK government announced a new Fundamental AI Research Lab backed by up to £40 million over six years, plus substantial computing access worth tens of millions of pounds
Lab will target fundamental AI limitations including hallucinations, unreliable memory, and unpredictable reasoning to create more accurate and trustworthy systems
Part of the broader UKRI AI Strategy allocating £1.6 billion over four years for AI research
Peer review panel chaired by Raia Hadsell, Vice President of Research at Google DeepMind and DSIT AI Ambassador
Research areas include improving medical diagnostics, building resilient infrastructure, accelerating scientific discovery, and enhancing public service tools
Framed as a push for UK 'sovereign AI' to reduce reliance on American technology companies like Google, Anthropic, and OpenAI

stories.headline: OpenAI's GPT-5 runs 36,000 experiments in Ginkgo Bioworks autonomous lab, cuts protein costs 40%
key_facts: Ginkgo Bioworks and OpenAI demonstrated a closed-loop autonomous lab where GPT-5 designed, executed, analyzed, and refined 36,000 cell-free protein synthesis experiments over six iterative cycles
The system achieved a 40% reduction in protein production cost and 57% improvement in reagent cost versus state of the art, producing superfolder GFP at $422 per gram
GPT-5 was given internet access, a computer with data analysis packages, and experimental metadata, operating like an experimental scientist with minimal human intervention
Ginkgo's cloud laboratory in Boston uses reconfigurable automation carts (RAC) and Catalyst automation software for physical execution
The preprint was released February 5, 2026 on bioRxiv, sparking debate over whether chatbot-controlled robots could replace human biologists
Ginkgo is now commercially selling the AI-improved reaction mix in its reagents store, demonstrating commercial viability of AI-driven science

stories.headline: ICLR 2026 workshop marks recursive self-improvement's shift from theory to deployed systems
key_facts: The ICLR 2026 Workshop on AI with Recursive Self-Improvement brings together researchers to build algorithmic foundations for reliable self-improving AI systems

Workshop organizers note RSI has moved from thought experiments to deployed systems: LLM agents rewriting their own codebases, scientific discovery pipelines scheduling continual fine-tuning, and robotics stacks patching controllers from streaming telemetry
Contributions organized around five lenses: change targets inside the system, temporal regime of adaptation, mechanisms and drivers, operating contexts, and evidence of improvement
Workshop covers self-improvement across experience learning, synthetic data pipelines, multimodal agentic systems, weak-to-strong generalization, and inference-time scaling
Author notifications were sent March 1, 2026 with public release of accepted papers; workshop takes place at ICLR 2026 in Singapore
Workshop is paradigm-agnostic: welcoming work on foundation models, agent frameworks, robots, learning algorithms, optimizers, control and program synthesis
